t: A group of walled city-kingdoms in northern Nigeria and southern Niger, including Kano, Katsina, Zazzau, Daura and Gobir.
They never united, but shared a language, court institutions and a trade network linking the Sahara and the forest.
The jihad of Usman dan Fodio (1804–1808) replaced their dynasties with the Fulani emirates of the Sokoto Caliphate.
dyk: The fine goatskin leather sold in Europe as ‘Morocco leather’ was largely tanned and dyed by Hausa craftsmen and carried across the Sahara.
ev: Bagauda becomes the first king of Kano, according to the Kano Chronicle
Wangarawa merchants bring Islam to Kano under Sarki Yaji
Muhammad Rumfa becomes king of Kano and reforms its government
Kanta Kotal of Kebbi throws off Songhai rule
Gobir destroys Birnin Zamfara, the capital of Zamfara
Usman dan Fodio’s followers defeat Gobir at Tabkin Kwotto
Alkalawa falls and Sarki Yunfa of Gobir is killed

f.capital: No common capital; chief cities Kano, Katsina, Zaria (Zazzau), Daura and Alkalawa (Gobir)
f.founder: Bagauda of Kano (traditionally); legendary ancestor Bayajidda
f.successor: Sokoto Caliphate; Abuja, Maradi and Tsibiri successor states
